statement.p: Calculate the flux of the vector field \vec F=(x^2+z^2)\vec j through the disk of radius 2 in the xz-plane and centered at the origin and oriented in the direction of the positive y axis.

static.solution: D, is in the xz-plane and oriented in the direction of the positive y axis, d\vec A=\vec j\, dx\, dz and \int_{D} \vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_{D} (x^2+z^2)\vec j\cdot \vec j\, dx\,dz = \int_{D}(x^2+z^2)\, dx\,dz. Using polar coordinates (with x = r\cos\theta and z = r\sin\theta), \int_{D}\vec F\cdot d\vec A = \int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{2} r^2\cdot r\, dr\,d\theta = 2\pi \left.\frac {r^4}4\right|_0^{2} = 8\pi.
